universities: Changchun University of Science and Technology; Qingdao University; Changchun University

notes: VERSION: version of record (physica status solidi RRL 20(1), e202500340, 9 PDF pages; published online 2026-01-30, received 2025-08-20), no supplement. Licence: Crossref lists the Wiley terms (vor) and TDM records only, no open licence; access not verified (unknown). NO DEVICE ROWS (convention dd): the paper is a microwave/HFSS and analytic model study of a c-axis BTO MZI modulator; its only measured data are electrical VNA S21 of the electrodes of three fabricated samples (0 to 40 GHz, Fig. 6(b)), and no Vpi, optical loss, extinction ratio, EO response or optical measurement is reported. The bandwidth statements are model outputs: microwave S21 about -2.7 dB at 60 GHz (Fig. 2(b), 9 structures), -3.0 to -5.2 dB at 60 GHz depending on electrode width and gap (Fig. 4(a)-(c)), a derived -6.4 dB microwave criterion for a -3 dB lightwave bandwidth (alpha_m L = 0.74, Eq. 14), and a modelled lightwave bandwidth that increases with the microwave frequency (53 GHz at 60 GHz for WE = 80 um, Fig. 4(d)). Source defects: the abstract claims a lightwave bandwidth of over 55 GHz while the body gives 53 GHz (p.6); text gives lengths 0.7, 1.0, 1.5 mm and Fig. 6 labels 0.72, 1.020, 1.52 mm; text puts S21 of the shortest device at -2.0 dB at 40 GHz while Fig. 6(b) shows about -1.0 dB for Device-720; Fig. 5 caption says both panels are Vb = 0 while the text assigns (b) to Vb = V_pi; text writes tSTO = 0.050 nm (read as 50 nm) and Gx = 80 um in one S21 sentence (read as 10 um, green curve); the text cites Figure 5c for the WE = 20 um S21 panel, which is Fig. 4(c) (Fig. 5 is the bit-energy figure). Model inputs (context_values in the evidence file): 450 nm BTO on 50 nm STO on SiO2 (1, 2, 3 um in the study), rib height 100 nm, rib width 4 um, electrodes labelled Au in the Fig. 1 caption and copper in the Fig. 2 and 4 captions, EO length 1 mm, r51 425 to 630 pm/V from earlier work. Fabrication facility and wafer source not named; Zhejiang University is acknowledged for measurement help only. Same-group earlier work (references 16, 24-27 of the paper) is not distilled here.

LN Pockels, flat over 0.1-330 GHz: r33 = 26.9 pm/V and 1/2(r13 + 2 r42) = 15.0 pm/V (linear fits; text p.5, Fig. 4a p.6). BTO Pockels (Fig. 4b p.6): r33 = 125 pm/V at 100 MHz, Debye fit gamma0 = 565 MHz, sigma = 0.06, S_R = 75 pm/V, r_inf = 60 pm/V (flat about 60 pm/V above about 1 GHz; the Fig. 4 caption attributes these Debye parameters to the r42 data while the text on p.6 attributes them to r33; text followed); 1/2(r13 + 2 r42) = 481 pm/V at 100 MHz falling to 191 pm/V at 330 GHz via Miller's rule with delta = 0.327 +/- 0.002 pm/V and n0 = 2.26 at 1550 nm (p.6, Eq. 5). Literature clamped coefficients used for the r_eff(theta) curves, not measured here (p.10): BTO r33 = 30, r42 = 560, r13 = 6 pm/V; LN r33 = 31, r42 = 18, r13 = 9 pm/V. SUPPLEMENT ADDITIONS (re-check 2026-10-05; no main-text value changes): LN validation of the impedance model uses literature eps_c = 27, eps_a = 45 with no fitted parameters (supplement p.5, Fig. S1), LN devices of 50, 100, 150 um (Fig. S2); EO characterization uses the 50 um LN and 25 um BTO shifters, each GSG electrode carries two shifters with separate grating couplers (supplement p.7-8, Fig. S4). Poling (supplement p.16-17, Fig. S8): DC bias raised in 1 V steps with a 50 GHz tone until the peak-sideband ratio saturated, bias removed, efficiency settles about 1 dB below the poled value; all measurements without bias because frequencies above 110 GHz precluded bias. Electrodes 200 nm (supplement p.12). Propagation loss about 20 dB/cm and 0.1 dB reflection give the approximately 0.2 dB insertion loss of a 50 um shifter (main p.2, simulation). Main text additions: 130 nm amorphous-Si grating couplers and 550 C O2 anneal for 1 h (p.9).
